Open-Meteo is enabled. Confirm again to apply changes.
Review the disclosure before enabling Open-Meteo.

SterSU will send the coordinates you entered to api.open-meteo.com over HTTPS to request current temperature, WMO weather code and day/night status. Open-Meteo also receives your network IP address. The optional display name stays on this device. Requests occur while the sidebar weather is visible, at the selected interval; the last result is cached locally. SterSU does not request device location permission or upload weather readings to its own server. Open-Meteo\'s Free API is for non-commercial use under its CC BY 4.0 terms; commercial use requires an appropriate plan. Weather data is attributed to Open-Meteo.com. See https://open-meteo.com/en/terms. Switch to Manual to stop future requests.
Enter valid decimal latitude (−90 to 90) and longitude (−180 to 180).

Xiaomi Weather is enabled. Confirm again to apply a new refresh interval.
Review the disclosure before enabling Xiaomi Weather.

SterSU will read the current temperature, weather description, city, weather type, temperature unit and publication time from the Xiaomi Weather app through its local ContentProvider. The Weather app may refresh data over the network and uses the location selected in that app. SterSU does not request device location for this feature or send this reading to a SterSU server. Queries run while the sidebar is visible, at the chosen interval. Xiaomi Weather must be installed and allow access. You can disable this at any time by choosing Manual.
Updates only while the weather widget is visible in the foreground. If a request fails, the last successful reading is marked as cached. Manual refreshes are limited to one every 10 seconds.
This is manually entered weather, not a live reading. Open Configure sidebar → Weather to choose Custom API, Xiaomi Weather, or Open-Meteo.
Connect an HTTPS GET endpoint returning a JSON object. Enter the city or coordinates in your endpoint URL as required by your provider. No location permission is requested.
Overrides the location returned by the API. This label is not sent with the request.
For Bearer authentication, enter Bearer followed by a space and your token. Leave both header fields empty if authentication is not required.

Example: {\"now\":{\"temp\":26,\"text\":\"Clear\"}} → temperature: now.temp, description: now.text. Nested fields and array indices such as results[0].now.temp are supported. Temperature must be a number or numeric string; description and location are optional text fields.
The last tested configuration stays active until new settings pass the test. Changes here are drafts.
Not enabled yet. Test and enable to save these settings and show online weather.

Requests go only to your configured service, which can see your IP address and the URL/header you enter. No device identifiers or automatic location are added. Keys stay in private app storage, separate from theme exports. Redirects and unencrypted HTTP are not allowed.

Use this page to configure the module unmount policy for selected application UIDs. It does not uninstall or disable apps, and does not guarantee that every Root trace is hidden.

1. Open Application hiding and search All apps. Filters can show system apps, risk hints, or policy states.
2. The switch explicitly enables or disables the policy. Expand Details to follow the global default again.
3. Check all affected packages when apps share a UID. Root-granted and protected UID groups cannot be changed here.
4. Fully stop and reopen the target app. The displayed status verifies configuration only, not the behavior of running processes.
5. Use the menu to preview an import, export policies, or restore the last automatic backup.

Use a normal path when you want to hide a file or directory. Use loop or map paths only when the matching SUSFS capability is shown on the page. Open Redirect replaces one path with another for the selected UID scheme.
The runtime page controls the SUSFS switch, logging, AVC log protection, and mount visibility. Kernel identity options are applied only when the device reports support.
Change a setting, then tap Save and apply. The page shows whether the change was applied, partially applied, or needs a reboot. Read the status message before leaving the page.
Do not hide /data/adb or its management folders globally. Keep a recovery path, change one option at a time, and export a backup before changing identity or mount rules.
The tool or kernel did not report the matching SUSFS capability, so the control is intentionally disabled.
Why does it say reboot required?
SUSFS cannot reliably remove some already-installed hooks or boot-time identity changes while Android is running.
Why are only some entries effective?
Check the per-entry error code. A path can be missing, late-mounted, unsupported, or rejected by the kernel; the service retries at boot.
Support depends on the installed kernel and tool reporting the capability. The manager does not claim support when the upstream SUSFS source or runtime probe is missing.
